questions.question: What is the generate-review-fix agent loop pattern?
choices: A workflow where AI generates code, another AI reviews it, and a human fixes issues manually
An autonomous cycle where an agent generates output, evaluates its own quality, and iteratively fixes issues until criteria are met
A deployment pipeline that generates builds, reviews logs, and fixes server errors
A testing strategy where tests are generated, reviewed by QA, and then code is fixed
questions.explanation: The generate-review-fix loop is an autonomous agent pattern: the agent generates output, critically reviews it against requirements or test results, and iteratively fixes problems — creating a self-improving cycle.

questions.question: Why is the review step essential in the generate-review-fix loop rather than just generating and fixing?
choices: The review step adds unnecessary complexity to the system
Review provides an objective evaluation that identifies issues the generation step might miss, preventing the agent from reinforcing its own errors
Review is only needed for code, not for other types of output
The review step is a legal requirement for all AI systems
questions.explanation: Without review, an agent may generate flawed output and attempt to fix it without understanding what's wrong. Review provides critical evaluation — using tests, validators, or a separate reasoning pass — to identify specific failures.

questions.question: What is the key risk of running the generate-review-fix loop without proper termination criteria?
choices: The loop will always converge on the perfect solution
The agent may loop indefinitely, wasting compute resources, or oscillate between solutions without converging
The model will run out of memory after exactly 10 iterations
There is no risk — the loop always improves quality with each iteration
questions.explanation: Without defined stopping conditions (max iterations, test pass threshold, or confidence score), the loop can run forever, oscillate between states, or waste resources on diminishing returns.
